summary: Safe, self-gated rewrite stage with no rules problems. But the mechanism is probably misattributed: the ~6 us ticket-vs-no-ticket gap at B=16 most likely comes from the end-of-kernel serial merge tail, which DEFER keeps and may make worse, not from the in-loop round trip. Expect a neutral result unless prepare's variant matrix shows otherwise. No companions.
justification: The target is real. Full decode_16 is 111.1 us (kernel 110.1 us, floor 63.2 us) and decode_32 is 226.4 us (kernel 225.6 us, floor 126.4 us). Both are weight-16 rows. The [sk-diag] gap of ~6 us at B=16 and ~3 us at B=32 between <4,ticket> and <4,no ticket> is cited from logs. The 'expected' directions agree with TASK.md: faster on full decode_16/32, flat elsewhere, and B=1 TWO stays untouched. Now the structure. In master's single-level path (submission.py ~1338-1402), a CTA's segments are its head segment (the tail of request b, from c_hi's view), any number of whole requests (finalized in place, no ticket), and its tail segment (the start of request b+1). So each CTA makes at most ONE in-loop non-whole arrival: the head segment, which ends mid-loop. The tail segment already ends at n == N-1. All CTAs start together with near-equal tile counts. For a request spanning c_lo..c_hi, c_lo and the interior CTAs finish at loop end, while c_hi's head segment ends early. So c_hi's mid-loop arrival is essentially never the last one: mid-loop work is one __threadfence + 2 __syncthreads + atomicAdd, roughly sub-us, and merge_slots never runs mid-loop in practice. The 'serial merge_slots of ~16 slots while the next segment's tiles wait' that the hypothesis describes therefore does not happen on the critical path. The merge runs at the END of the last-finishing CTA, where it forms the kernel tail: merge_range walks ~16 slots serially through L2, then finalize_store. DEFER does not remove that tail. It can lengthen it: c_hi now arrives at the end too, so it becomes a candidate last arriver for BOTH b (head) and b+1 (tail) and could run two serial merges back-to-back. WEAKEST LINK: the 6 us gap is attributed to in-loop fences with no measurement that separates the fence/atomic cost from the end-merge tail. Realistic gain if the hypothesis is right: about 0.5-1 us per CTA's single mid-loop fence, below the 1.02x (~2.2 us at B=16) routing margin. So the most likely outcome is PATH CHOSEN = master, i.e. flat. That is cheap and still informative, but only if prepare also prints the numbers. Design nit that can break correctness/routing: the claim 'a CTA holds <= 3 segments for B<=64, assert it' holds only for the scored ~80K-context shapes. The landed self-check cases (B=64 mixed at grid 7, B=2 [20000,2] at grid 7, B=32 ragged at grid 3) and test shapes such as batch 4 spread mixed page 1 give one CTA many segments. The smem list only ever needs the NON-WHOLE segments, which are <= 1 deferred by construction (<= 2 counting the tail). Assert or size on that count, not on total segments, or the self-check falls back or traps on cases that are fine.
confounders: full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (master, c3c1b01): shares the splitkv_attn_sk_kernel template. DEFER is only on the single-level TICKET && !TWO branch, so the B=1 two-level path must stay byte-identical. Any change to the shared prologue or template instantiation would move full decode_1 and contaminate the read. Check that the kernel row for full decode_1 stays at ~18.6 us.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv (stage-1 A+B, landed): only the [sk-diag] baseline uses it now, not the timed path. It does not confound the kernel-row read, but its A+B number is a useful sanity anchor in the prepare log.

fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads-launch-cleanup: _pre_attention_kernel (2.0-2.2 us) runs before the sk kernel on the same rows and stays unchanged. The headline shape time includes it, so read the sk kernel's own row, not the shape total.
Headline noise: recent full-decode stages repeatedly showed 'lost/gained on sliding verify_1/decode_1' with no code change there. A sliding-row move on this run is noise, not interaction.
interference: No companion is warranted. This is a kind: rewrite stage judged on the sk kernel's own top_kernels row, and the hypothesis already carries an in-prepare A/B: DEFER on/off x grid 2xSM/SM at B=16/32/64, interleaved graph replay, with both numbers printed in PATH CHOSEN. That A/B is the disambiguator, and it costs no check. A loss cannot reach the headline because the gate falls back to master's variant 0. A gain is attributable on the kernel row. Attention has 8 checks for 8 queued hypotheses, so spending one on a companion is not justified. Better than a companion, at zero check cost: add one extra [sk-diag] row timing <4,ticket> with the merge+finalize skipped by the last arriver (diag only, never routed). The prepare log then splits the 6 us gap into in-loop fence cost versus end-merge tail, which tells the next stage whether to attack the tail (parallel or wider merge_range loads, or distributing the final merge across the arriving CTAs) instead of the fences.
rules_flags: None blocking. Routing on prepare-time timing is outside the timed call and follows the landed pattern. Ticket arrays stay self-resetting, hold no data, and need no device pointer into state tensors.

Correctness detail: with deferred arrival, the single post-loop __threadfence must come after ALL partial stores for every recorded entry, and before each atomicAdd. The last arriver needs an acquire __threadfence (or atom.acq_rel as in ticket_arrive) before merge_slots. Keep the per-entry __syncthreads + flag_s broadcast so the merge stays uniform.

Do not use a device-side assert/trap for the segment-count bound. A trap kills the context during the judge's test shapes. Size the smem list for the provable bound (non-whole segments <= 2) so no runtime check is needed.
open_questions: Is the [sk-diag] 'no ticket' number kernel-only, and was it measured on the same cold-L2 interleaved replay as the ticket variant? If not, part of the 6 us may be measurement asymmetry.
How long does merge_slots + finalize_store take for ~16 slots, measured as the tail of the last CTA? That is the likely real cost, and a stage that parallelizes it may be the better stage 4.
Under DEFER, how often does one CTA become last arriver for two requests (head and tail) and run two serial merges at the end? Print the count in the self-check if cheap.
